reviewScope: Twenty moderate tasks and one hundred actual language bodies, including per-language ordered-map/dictionary-list LRU cache state.

questions.algorithm: Three XOR assignments exchange independent local operands before returning their final values.
questions.review: Read all five bodies: exactly two swap variables, no tuple/destructuring swap, reversed-pair shortcut or temporary. The returned collection is allocated only after the exchange. Values are independent function arguments, matching the public local-variable task; caller aliasing is not invented. Equal values, zeros and opposite signed endpoints are executed; no arithmetic-overflow assumption is used.

questions.algorithm: Build one normalized-word frequency dictionary and answer a batch of lookups.
questions.review: Read all five actual bodies. C# uses invariant lowercase and ordinal dictionary keys; Java uses Locale.ROOT, Python/JS lowercase operations are equivalent on the explicit ASCII domain, and C++ converts only ASCII A..Z. Query lookups do not decrement counts. Both arrays stay readonly, and repeated queries retain their original positions. Independent direct per-query scans cover exhaustive small token lists, absent words, mixed case, repeated queries and 1000-token/query bounds.

questions.algorithm: Inspect every full row, column and two corner diagonals of a generic square board.
questions.review: Input encoding explicitly distinguishes empty from the two players. All five bodies reject an empty candidate line and preserve board outer/row identity. Every n<=3 board with at most one winning player is tested, including states not constrained by move-history validation. Larger n=50 bounds and partial lines verify that generic wins require a full n-cell line. No dual-winner tie rule is invented.

questions.algorithm: Repeated quotient division by five accumulates the prime-five valuation of n!.
questions.review: No factorial or growing fixed-width power is computed. The independently authored oracle directly inspects factorial decimal endings for small n and uses arbitrary-precision powers for large n. Boundaries around every representable power of five and int.MaxValue are executed. JavaScript uses Math.floor rather than real division; all totals fit signed int.

questions.algorithm: Sort private copies and advance the smaller endpoint while recording exact widened differences.
questions.review: Read all five bodies and signatures. C#/Java widen the first operand to long before subtraction; C++ uses long long before subtraction; Python int and bounded JS Number are exact. The widest difference 4294967295 is admitted and actually executed. Empty inputs return -1. Copy sorting preserves original arrays. A cross-product absolute-difference oracle independently checks all small pair combinations and maximum-length/signed-endpoint cases. Java observation supports Long and Python/JS wide-result validation retains strict integer typing.

questions.algorithm: Choose by operand sign when signs differ and by wrapped difference sign only when signs agree, then select the original operand.
questions.review: Read all five bodies: no comparison operator, if/switch, conditional expression or max/min helper appears in the solution. C#/Java/JS explicitly observe 32-bit difference bits; Python masks to 32 bits. C++ subtraction uses uint32_t, not overflowing signed subtraction, and chooses via 0/1 products of exact original operands rather than unsigned-to-signed narrowing. Extreme opposite signs and all small signed pairs are executed against host max.

questions.algorithm: Iteratively spell nonzero three-digit groups and scales, reverse groups, join once and apply the original sign.
questions.review: Read all five bodies and number-name tables. C#/Java/C++ widen the input before negating its minimum signed value; Python and JS represent that magnitude exactly. Zero groups are omitted, teens are not split into tens/ones, and joining nonempty groups prevents trailing/doubled spaces. Zero is handled separately. An independent largest-scale recursive oracle checks every -1001..2000 value, scale boundaries, zero gaps, random signed values and both endpoints. The returned title-case/no-and convention is explicit.

questions.algorithm: Unit-addition sign reversal; signed repeated-addend multiplication and signed whole-divisor removal.
questions.review: Read all five bodies. No subtraction, variable unary negation, multiplication, division, remainder, bit arithmetic or abs helper performs user arithmetic. Only the allowed negative unit literal and addition are used. Java local Negator, C# local function, C++ lambda and Python/JS nested function implement the same explicit unit invariant. Multiplication chooses its signed addend before looping, avoiding a product-sized sign-reversal loop. Division accumulates signed quotient units and truncates toward zero. Static operator checks are only restriction evidence; actual cases independently execute all small signed pairs, zero factors, negative division and admitted endpoints against ordinary host arithmetic. The bounded repeated-addition domain is explicit, not a claim of efficient full-width integer arithmetic.

questions.algorithm: Accumulate birth/death-after-year deltas, then retain the first strictly maximal population prefix.
questions.review: All five use 102 zero counters for 101 admitted years plus the final sentinel. Decrement occurs at death+1, preserving the inclusive death year. Strict best updates retain earliest ties and return 1900 for no people. Independent direct population counting covers small lifetime multisets, repeated people, same-year lifetimes and year 2000.

questions.algorithm: Enumerate long-plank count once in increasing order; collapse equal plank lengths to one total.
questions.review: Each actual body emits n+1 strictly increasing lengths only when lengths differ. Zero planks returns [0]. C#/Java allocate exact int arrays, JavaScript uses Array.from, Python a concrete comprehension and C++ reserves a vector. The bound ensures every product/sum is at most 10^9. The independent small oracle builds reachable length sets by repeated plank addition.

questions.algorithm: Count exact hits, then consume only unmatched secret-color frequencies for unmatched guesses.
questions.review: All five bodies use the same four-color alphabet order consistently for both passes. A hit is excluded from the frequency table and from pseudo-hit consumption; repeated guesses cannot consume one slot twice. Independent permutation matching of unmatched positions, all-color strings, monochrome guesses, reversals, rotations and two-color exhaustive pairs cover multiplicity errors.

questions.algorithm: Locate the last prefix-maximum violation and the first suffix-minimum violation without sorting or mutating input.
questions.review: Strict comparisons treat equal values as already ordered. Empty input is checked before indexing; no forward violation returns [-1,-1]. All five return inclusive original endpoints and preserve input. Independent sorted-copy mismatch endpoints agree for all small repeated-value arrays, signed extremes and 10000-element sorted/reverse inputs.

questions.algorithm: Keep the best nonnegative suffix sum and global maximum in one scan.
questions.review: Empty/all-negative input returns zero, as in the author source; a nonempty-only variant is not substituted. The oracle directly enumerates contiguous intervals. The shared domain bounds all sums by 10^9, so Java/C#/C++ arithmetic and JS Number results are exact. Python arbitrary precision does not hide a cross-language overflow. Inputs are not modified.

questions.algorithm: Enumerate a replacement length, derive the other from symbol counts and verify consistent text slices without expansion.
questions.review: Read all five actual bodies. Missing a symbols use one candidate length zero; missing b requires zero remaining text. The first assigned empty substring is distinguished from an unassigned null/flag, so empty and equal mappings remain legal. Total length is checked before scanning, and final offset must consume all text. C#/Java slices and C++ substr bounds follow that equation. An independent memoized assignment-backtracking oracle covers all small binary patterns/texts, single-symbol nondivisible lengths, empty values and maximum bounds. Boolean observations reject numeric stand-ins.

questions.algorithm: Iterative eight-neighbor water component counting with a separate visited matrix; sort all component sizes preserving duplicates.
questions.review: Every language marks water at discovery, preserves elevations and input row identities, and explores diagonals. Python/JS allocate independent visited rows, C# uses a rectangular Boolean table, Java Boolean rows, C++ nested vector<bool>. Each cell enters one work stack once. Independent DSU unions establish components, including all binary 3x3 grids, all-water 50x50, diagonal-only links and equal-sized separate ponds. Sorting p sizes is included in the time bound.

questions.algorithm: Scan dictionary entries in order and compare each letter through a fixed 26-letter keypad map.
questions.review: Read all five actual bodies and all 26 mapping entries, especially four-letter groups pqrs and wxyz. Length is tested before character matching; digits 0/1 and empty digits cannot match the nonempty-word domain. Returned entries preserve original order and duplicate occurrences. C++ returns copied string values; other languages retain immutable word references. An independent inverse digit-to-letter-group oracle checks every letter, short combinations and the 1000-entry/20-character bounds.

questions.algorithm: Derive the necessary half-sum difference and scan original first order against second-value membership.
questions.review: Read all five bodies. Signed 64-bit totals or exact wider host numbers avoid overflowing sums. Odd difference exits without integer-division mistakes, including negative values. C#/Java/C++ check candidate range before narrowing; Python/JS membership cannot match a wider nonexistent value. Inputs remain unchanged. Earliest-first-occurrence convention matches the public scan; empty arrays cannot supply a swap. Independent nested candidate exchange sums verify every answer, including a counterexample where narrowing would wrap into a false membership hit.

questions.algorithm: Sparse black-cell membership, turn/toggle/move simulation, visited extrema and final rectangular rendering.
questions.review: Read all five bodies. Python stores coordinate tuples; C#/Java/C++/JS encode coordinates within the proven range [-steps,steps] using width 2*steps+1 and an offset, so distinct coordinates cannot collide. The largest key for steps=2000 fits signed 32-bit and JS exact integers. Right/down/left/up direction indices match row-down coordinates. Bounds update after every move and retain erased white positions. The final marker overlays color. An independent dense byte-board oracle rotates a direction vector instead of indexing the reference direction table, checking 0..100 steps and 200/500/1000/2000 bounds. Hand traces through the first black-cell turn disambiguate operation order.

questions.algorithm: Sort a private copy and greedily consume matching smallest/largest remaining occurrences.
questions.review: Read the two public variants and explicitly selected disjoint-occurrence semantics; this is not all index-pair enumeration. All five reference bodies widen sums before comparing, consume both endpoints on a match, and normalize/order pairs by their sorted walk. Equal values require two occurrences; repeated pairs remain repeated. A count-by-complement-class oracle independently calculates maximum multiplicities. Executed exhaustive short inputs, odd equal counts, 1000 repeated values and signed-endpoint overflow counterexamples.

questions.algorithm: Per-instance key index with least-to-most-recent order; successful Get and every Set refresh, with oldest eviction only after a new overflow.
questions.review: Read all five actual implementations and language-specific WHY notes. C# indexes stable LinkedListNode tuple entries and moves the same node. C++ indexes list iterators and splices without iterator invalidation. Java LinkedHashMap explicitly enables accessOrder, Python OrderedDict explicitly moves existing keys and JavaScript Map deletes/reinserts because get alone does not refresh. Nullable string/optional return types distinguish missing from a stored empty string. Constructor capacity and data are instance-owned. A separate plain-list-order oracle checks all short action sequences at capacities 1/2/3, replacement, refresh, absent reads, signed-endpoint keys, quoted/backslash strings and maximum capacity/transcript length. Typed method assertions and dynamic exact string/null checks enforce the API. Five deliberately corrupted implementations without Get refresh are executed as negative regressions; structural metadata is not credited as execution.

languageBindingReview.csharp: Read all actual signed-int bodies. Array return expressions match int[] signatures. NumberMax uses uint sign extraction and an explicit unchecked difference, then signed masks; no conditional comparison helper. MasterMind IndexOf uses the admitted ASCII alphabet. Mutable array inputs are read only in this batch. New closest-difference results are long; subtraction and pair totals widen before arithmetic. Invariant token keys and private array clones preserve contracts. English magnitude is long before negation; local nonempty word groups join with exact spaces. Nullable mapping strings distinguish unassigned from empty. T9 returns List<string> matching its visible signature. Addition-only arithmetic uses a visible local helper with unit increments. Ant rendering uses HashSet<int> coordinate keys and StringBuilder rows. LRU Get uses Func<int,string?> and Set Action<int,string> in the judge. Nodes retain their dictionary identities during movement and replacement; capacity eviction removes both the first list node and its index.
languageBindingReview.javascript: Read all actual functions. Factorial division is floored, NumberMax bit operations coerce the intended signed 32-bit patterns, and bounded ordinary arithmetic stays exactly representable. All array results are materialized, not generators. Inputs remain unchanged. New widened results use Number.isSafeInteger and the admitted exact range. Numeric sort comparators avoid lexical sorting; Map/Set and copied arrays preserve inputs. English magnitude uses exact Number arithmetic with Math.floor divisions. Pattern null differs from empty, matching results require boolean type, and T9 preserves duplicate entries in a concrete array. Addition-only arithmetic uses unit additions rather than Math helpers or bitwise shortcuts. Ant numeric coordinate keys remain exact and output arrays preserve every row. LRU Get must return string or null, while Set undefined becomes transcript null. Map get is followed by delete/set, and replacements also refresh without a duplicate key.
languageBindingReview.python: Read all actual function bodies and exact annotations. NumberMax masks the potentially wider difference before extracting its 32-bit sign; the signed selection mask works with arbitrary-width bitwise operations. Arrays are concrete lists and bool is not an integer observation. The admitted numeric bounds remain shared. New closest-difference observations allow the exact widened result without accepting bool; pair observations validate nested integer rows. Sorted copies preserve caller lists. Text/bool observation branches apply only to their actual return kinds, leaving integer strictness intact. English floor division consumes chunks; pattern None differs from empty; T9 yields a concrete list. Addition-only arithmetic does not call abs or built-in arithmetic helpers. Ant positions use tuple-set keys and independent mutable row builders; the result is a concrete string list. LRU Get returns only str or None and Set only None. OrderedDict membership distinguishes absent from empty strings; move_to_end is explicit on both successful operations.
languageBindingReview.cpp: Read all actual methods with const vector/string references. NumberMax difference is uint32_t and final operand multiplication by 0/1 cannot overflow. No undefined signed subtraction or implementation-defined unsigned narrowing is used. Returned vectors own their values; prefix/suffix scans index only nonempty input. New dictionary/set headers are explicit. long long arithmetic precedes differences/sums and range checks precede narrowing; all original vectors remain const. English magnitude widens before negation and reverse iteration joins groups. Pattern assignment uses separate haveA/haveB flags so empty strings are valid mappings; T9 output strings own their copies. Addition-only arithmetic uses a nonrecursive lambda; bounded sums stay signed-safe. Ant membership uses unordered_set<int>, with declared table headers and owned string rows. LRU Get returns optional<string>, checked with static_assert, and Set returns void. Visible list/optional/iterator headers support the actual class; splice leaves indexed iterators valid.
languageBindingReview.java: Read all actual methods. Integer arithmetic uses justified bounds, except the intentionally wrapping subtraction whose bit pattern is observed with >>>. Returned int[] arrays match declared types, String indexing uses charAt, and the frequency table is local per call. Inputs are unchanged. New closest-difference results are long and the JSON encoder handles Long. Locale.ROOT fixes token normalization; sum candidates are range-checked before int conversion. English magnitude is long, groups reverse locally, and String.join emits no extra spaces. Pattern matching uses String.equals and Boolean encoding; T9 returns materialized List<String>. Addition-only arithmetic uses a local Negator class with no forbidden arithmetic. Ant coordinate keys are collision-free ints; StringBuilder rows retain visited bounds. LRU public Get returns String and Set returns void, checked reflectively. accessOrder=true refreshes successful get and replacement put; the first surviving key iterator entry is evicted after overflow.

remainingAcceptance: remaining known collection content and classification
